questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Repeated Integrals Using the Sum and Product Rules
questions.worked_solution:
Since the domain of integration $R=[1,4]\times [0,2]\times [0,\pi /2]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,dx\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\,dx{\int }_{0}^{2}\,dy{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}\,dx{\int }_{0}^{2}\,dy{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,dz & =(4-1)\cdot (2-0)\cdot [\operatorname{sin}⁡z]_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =3\cdot 2\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =6\cdot (1-0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Repeated Integrals Using the Sum and Product Rules
questions.worked_solution:
Since the domain of integration $R=[0,4]\times [1,2]\times [0,1]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}x{y}^{2}{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{4}x\,dx{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,dy{\int }_{0}^{1}{z}^{3}\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}x\,dx{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,dy{\int }_{0}^{1}{z}^{3}\,dz & ={[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{4}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{1}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{4}{z}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(8-0)\cdot (\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{3})\cdot (\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =8\cdot \frac{7}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{14}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Repeated Integrals Using the Sum and Product Rules
questions.worked_solution:
Since the domain of integration $R=[0,2]\times [0,e]\times [0,1]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{e}{e}^{-z}\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}dx{\int }_{0}^{e}dy{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{-z}\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}dx{\int }_{0}^{e}dy{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{-z}\,dz & =(2-0)\cdot (e-0)\cdot [-{e}^{-z}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =2\cdot e\cdot (-{e}^{-1}+{e}^{0}) \\  & =2e(1-{e}^{-1}) \\  & =2e-2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Repeated Integrals Over Non-Rectangular Domains
questions.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-y}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{x}2{e}^{z+1}\,dz\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-y}^{0}[{\int }_{0}^{x}2{e}^{z+1}\,dz]dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-y}^{0}2[{e}^{z+1}]_{z=0}^{z=x}\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-y}^{0}2({e}^{x+1}-e)\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-y}^{0}2({e}^{x+1}-e)\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[2{\int }_{-y}^{0}{e}^{x+1}-e\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2[{e}^{x+1}-ex]_{x=-y}^{x=0}\,dy \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{0+1}-e(0)-({e}^{-y+1}-e(-y))dy \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}e-{e}^{1-y}-ey\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{\int }_{0}^{1}e-{e}^{1-y}-ey\,dy & =2{[ey+{e}^{1-y}-\frac{e}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =2(e(1-0)+{e}^{1-1}-{e}^{1-0}-\frac{e}{2}({1}^{2}-{0}^{2})) \\  & =2(e+1-e-\frac{e}{2}) \\  & =2-e\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Repeated Integrals Over Non-Rectangular Domains
questions.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}{\int }_{0}^{y}xyz\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}[{\int }_{0}^{y}xyz\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}{[\frac{1}{2}xy{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{2}xy({y}^{2}-0)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{2}x{y}^{3}\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{2}x{y}^{3}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{2}x{y}^{3}\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{8}x{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{8}x({x}^{4}-0)\,dx \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{5}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{5}\,dx & =\frac{1}{8}{[\frac{1}{6}{x}^{6}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{48}(64-0) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
